shipped_originals.title_o: The Benefit of Becoming Friends: Complaining after Service Failures Leads Customers with Strong Ties to Increase Loyalty

blind_target.evidence_quote: Claim for Review – The claim selected was that strongly tied customers who complain (vs. withhold feedback) after a service failure will increase their loyalty. In contrast, for weakly tied customers, complaining has no effect on loyalty.
blind_target.outcome_quote: Stage 2: H* was not supported as the interaction term on the overall ANOVA was not significant. In addition, the pattern of means in the strong ties group was not consistent but the pattern of means in the weak ties group was consistent.
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: Both completed stages explicitly reject support for the focal interaction. A consistent weak-ties mean pattern is ancillary to the central failed test. The final report identifies the target by project shorthand, but supplies no reference entry.

shipped_originals.title_o: The Impact of Resource Scarcity on Price-Quality Judgments

blind_target.title: The Impact of Resource Scarcity on Price-Quality Judgments
blind_target.evidence_quote: In this sixth installment of Data Replicada, we report our attempt to replicate a recently published Journal of Consumer Research (JCR) article entitled, “The Impact of Resource Scarcity on Price-Quality Judgments” ( .html ).
blind_target.outcome_quote: On the one hand, we were successful at dramatically reducing attrition. On the other hand, we were unsuccessful at reducing differential attrition, as once again many more participants dropped out of the Scarcity condition than the Control condition. So then we gave up, and decided to call the whole thing “inconclusive.”
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: Authors explicitly call the entire attempt inconclusive because differential attrition compromised random assignment and valid comparison, despite initial significant effects. Aggregate includes the additional attempts discussed in footnote 7.

shipped_originals.title_o: When the Wait Isn’t So Bad: The Interacting Effects of Website Delay, Familiarity, and Breadth

blind_target.evidence_quote: This study is an exact replication of an experiment investigating the impacts of website design on users’ ability to use a website and their opinion of the website (Galletta et al., 2006).
blind_target.outcome_quote: The replication confirms the importance of website design features, specifically delay, breadth, and familiarity on users’ ability to use and form an opinion of a website. However, the replication did not confirm the main finding, that it is the interplay of these three variables, i.e., cognitive cost, that predict performance and attitude.
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: Explicit agreement and disagreement with the target findings; main interaction finding unconfirmed, but the title does not focus specifically on that interaction.

shipped_originals.title_o: High-Frequency Transcranial Random Noise Stimulation Enhances Perception of Facial Identity

blind_target.authors: Barbieri, M., Negrini, M., Nitsche, M. A., and Rivolta, D.
blind_target.title: Anodal-tDCS over the human right occipital cortex enhances the perception and memory of both faces and objects
blind_target.evidence_quote: Thus, in the current study we conducted two experiments where we sought to replicate recent findings (Romanska et al., 2015;Barbieri et al., 2016) reporting enhanced face perception following transcranial electrical stimulation techniques. The primary aim of Experiment 1 was to replicate enhancements in face perception following anodal tDCS compared to sham stimulation, which were observed with a medium effect size and group sample sizes of 16 (Barbieri et al., 2016).
blind_target.outcome_quote: In sum, the current results failed to replicate previous findings of enhanced face perception using anodal tDCS (Experiment 1) and high-frequency tRNS (Experiment 2) targeting the occipitotemporal cortex.
